sections.changelog:
Fixed

  • **The suggestions dropdown now ranks a wide pool and shows a narrow one.** The passes that refine an order — phrase proximity, model variant, product type — only reorder the rows they are handed, and the dropdown handed them exactly as many rows as it meant to display. Asking for ten meant ranking ten rows already sorted by relevance, so a rule with nothing to work on produced nothing. Measured on a 13 000-product catalogue: "battery iPhone 13" opened with nine plain models when the pool was fifty and with three when it was ten — the same query, the same rule, a pool too small to rank inside. The head is now scanned to the bound those passes are capped at anyway and cut to the requested size once they have all had it, so a small request names a display size rather than a ranking one. Two side effects on the same catalogue: the dropdown no longer loses rows to the product-type filter working on a truncated pool ("battery iPhone 13 max" 7 → 9 suggestions, "display" 6 → 9), and full-coverage share in the top ten never dropped across eighteen control queries. A third one is smaller and older: the adaptive floor and the typo rescue decide by how few rows a pass returned, and a request for one or two rows used to report the scarcity its own `LIMIT` clause had invented — those counts are now real. The results page, which already asks for a thousand rows, is unchanged. Costs 20 ms on a 377 ms search and no extra queries: the head is primed in one call, as it already was.
